title: Feature-Based Explainability of Transformer Scoring Models: A Fidelity-First Framework for Automated Writing Assessment
abstract: arXiv:2611.33175v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Transformer-based automated writing scoring models can achieve strong agreement with human scores while providing limited transparency into the response characteristics associated with their predictions. This study evaluated a feature-based post-hoc explanation approach in which explanatory fidelity was established before feature importance was interpreted. English Language Arts responses from three writing prompts in Grades 6 and 8 were analyzed, with about 12,700 responses per prompt and separate DeBERTa-v3-base research models for Expression and Conventions. Each response was represented by 61 interpretable linguistic and writing-quality features. Four approaches - theory-driven composites, hierarchical feature groupings, exploratory factor analysis, and Random Forest surrogates - were compared in their ability to reproduce DeBERTa predictions. Random Forest surrogates produced the largest observed R2 values across all six prompt-by-t

translated_title: Transformer评分模型的特征可解释性：一种面向自动写作评估的“保真度优先”框架
translated_abstract: 基于Transformer的自动写作评分模型虽然能够与人类评分达到高度一致，但对其预测所对应的写作响应特征缺乏透明度。本研究评估了一种基于特征的事后解释方法，该方法在解读特征重要性之前，先确立解释的保真度。研究分析了六年级和八年级三个写作题目的英语语言艺术写作响应，每个题目约12,700份响应，并针对“表达”和“规范”两个维度分别训练了独立的DeBERTa-v3-base研究模型。每份响应由61个可解释的语言和写作质量特征来表示。研究比较了四种方法——理论驱动的复合特征、层次化特征分组、探索性因子分析以及随机森林代理模型——在复现DeBERTa预测方面的能力。结果表明，随机森林代理模型在全部六个题目-维度组合上均产生了最高的观测R²值。
tldr: 本研究提出一种“保真度优先”的事后解释框架，通过61个可解释的语言与写作质量特征，比较四种解释方法对DeBERTa写作评分模型预测的复现能力，发现随机森林代理模型保真度最高，从而在确保解释忠实于模型预测之后再解读特征重要性，提升了自动写作评估的透明度。
en_tdlr: This study proposes a fidelity-first post-hoc explainability framework for transformer-based automated writing assessment, comparing four feature-based explanation approaches for DeBERTa scoring models using 61 interpretable linguistic features, and finding that Random Forest surrogates achieve the highest fidelity in reproducing model predictions.
